prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's density relaxation is gated only on *global* overflow, but the TNS cost comes from cells being pushed into *locally* congested bins; making the HPWL-driven density relaxation conditional on the *worst-region* density (not just aggregate overflow) — i.e. relax the density weight only when both total overflow is non-increasing AND the maximum per-bin density is not growing — keeps density pressure where it is actually needed without starving wirelength globally.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.270 robust(mean-std)=+0.057 min_case=+0.044 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.044 dWNS=+3.1% dTNS=+5.2% overflow~117
  bp-ng45: score=+0.118 dWNS=+13.2% dTNS=+11.4% overflow~100
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.108 dWNS=+6.9% dTNS=+13.7% overflow~108
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: gating density relaxation on worst-region density improved all three cases (total +0.270, robust +0.057, all valid). Gains concentrate in TNS (bp-ng45 +11.4%, bp_fe-ng45 +13.7%) with WNS also up, consistent with the mechanism—retaining density pressure in locally congested bins stops cells being displaced into already-tight regions, reducing the TNS-driving pushes without globally starving wirelength. ariane133-ng45 moved least (+0.044), plausibly because its overflow (~117) is already high, leaving less headroom. Next step: sweep the worst-region density growth threshold (e.g., allow small positive growth vs. strict non-growth) to test sensitivity and confirm the effect isn't threshold-specific.
